samples.summary: Login no longer always prints the OAuth URL; the documented headless copy-paste path now depends on `open()` rejecting
samples.evidence: `docs/design/cli.md:176` still describes step 3 of the login flow as "Opens browser: GET /auth/github?mode=cli&port=<port>&cliState=<nonce> (also prints URL for copy-paste in headless environments)". The diff removed the unconditional `console.error('If the browser does not open, visit the URL above.')` and now prints the *full* URL only inside the `catch` of `await open(oauthUrl)` (packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:78-87), while the always-printed line (login.ts:74-76) deliberately omits the nonce and is therefore unusable for copy-paste. `open()` resolves as soon as the launcher child is spawned, so on a headless box where `xdg-open`/`wslview` exists but fails afterwards (or opens on another display), nothing rejects, no usable URL is ever printed, and the login simply blocks until the 30-second timeout. The design doc (and the same claim at cli.md:212-214, which assumes the failure is always observable as a rejection) is left describing behaviour the code no longer guarantees. Fix belongs on the new code in login.ts (print the nonce-bearing URL unconditionally, or gate on an explicit `--no-browser`/TTY check) or on cli.md:176.

samples.summary: Agent-facing command schema for `login` not updated with the new `--allow-unbound-callback` flag
samples.evidence: `packages/cli/src/schema/registry.ts:43-50` is the machine-readable contract `wafflebase schema` publishes for agents; the `login` entry lists only `'--server'` under `parameters`. The diff adds a new user-visible option `--allow-unbound-callback` (packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:17-21) which is now the *only* way to log in against a server that predates the nonce echo, but an agent reading the schema cannot discover it. Nothing in the schema test (`packages/cli/test/schema.test.ts`) asserts parameter completeness, so this stays silent.

samples.summary: Published user docs for `wafflebase login` not updated for the new default-fail against older servers
samples.evidence: `packages/documentation/developers/cli.md:19-31` documents `wafflebase login` as "The CLI opens your browser for GitHub authentication and stores the JWT session…" with no mention that, as of this change, a login against a backend that does not echo `cliState` now fails with `The server completed the login but did not echo this invocation's nonce…` and requires `--allow-unbound-callback` (packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:216-220). Self-hosters following `packages/documentation/developers/self-hosting.md` (which pins an older backend deployment) are exactly the affected audience, and neither user-facing doc mentions the flag; only `docs/design/cli.md:220-227` does.

samples.summary: The empty-`WAFFLEBASE_CHANGED_AREAS` fail-safe test now returns via the push-to-main short-circuit and no longer exercises the guard it protects
samples.evidence: `resolve()` checks `env.WAFFLEBASE_CHANGED_AREAS` truthiness first (scripts/changed-areas.mjs:510) — an empty string falls through — and then short-circuits on `GITHUB_EVENT_NAME === 'push' && GITHUB_REF_NAME === 'main'` (scripts/changed-areas.mjs:530-534). By adding those two env vars, the modified test now always returns from line 530, so `out.full === true` and the new `/push to main/` reason assertion would hold even if the empty-string fall-through regressed (e.g. if `''` were ever parsed and returned as a zero-lane resolution). The regression guard described in the test's own comment is now vacuous; a stable non-main env (e.g. `GITHUB_EVENT_NAME: 'push', GITHUB_REF_NAME: 'topic'` with no diff base) would keep it meaningful.

finding.summary: Login no longer always prints the OAuth URL; the documented headless copy-paste path now depends on `open()` rejecting
finding.evidence: `docs/design/cli.md:176` still describes step 3 of the login flow as "Opens browser: GET /auth/github?mode=cli&port=<port>&cliState=<nonce> (also prints URL for copy-paste in headless environments)". The diff removed the unconditional `console.error('If the browser does not open, visit the URL above.')` and now prints the *full* URL only inside the `catch` of `await open(oauthUrl)` (packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:78-87), while the always-printed line (login.ts:74-76) deliberately omits the nonce and is therefore unusable for copy-paste. `open()` resolves as soon as the launcher child is spawned, so on a headless box where `xdg-open`/`wslview` exists but fails afterwards (or opens on another display), nothing rejects, no usable URL is ever printed, and the login simply blocks until the 30-second timeout. The design doc (and the same claim at cli.md:212-214, which assumes the failure is always observable as a rejection) is left describing behaviour the code no longer guarantees. Fix belongs on the new code in login.ts (print the nonce-bearing URL unconditionally, or gate on an explicit `--no-browser`/TTY check) or on cli.md:176.

verdict.reason: The code is as quoted (login.ts:71-76 prints a nonce-stripped URL unconditionally; login.ts:78-87 prints the full nonce-bearing URL only in the `catch` of `open()`), and docs/design/cli.md:176 does carry the loose "also prints URL for copy-paste in headless environments" line. But nothing here is blocking under the blast-radius rubric. (a) Grepping the repo for `Opening browser`, `Could not open a browser`, `no-browser`/`noBrowser`, `copy-paste`, `headless` finds no other code consumer of this print/URL contract — the only code hits are login.ts:75 and login.ts:83 themselves. No guard is bypassed, no signature/return shape/export is left referenced in an old form, no invariant another module assumes is violated. (b) The substantive half of the finding — that `open()` resolving on spawn leaves a headless box with no usable URL until the 30s timeout — is a judgement about the logic *inside* the diff (login.ts:78-87), which this lens explicitly defers to the correctness lens, and the doc-vs-code mismatch is spec fit, explicitly deferred to design-fit. (c) The only in-lane residue is "a doc left describing the old contract", which this lens's own scale prices as `minor`, not `major`; and the doc was in fact updated by the same change: docs/design/cli.md:211-218 states the new behaviour exactly ("the 'Opening browser' line prints the URL without it, and the full URL appears only when the browser could not be opened"), while cli.md:1177 ("Print the URL so user can copy-paste") is satisfied by the failure branch and cli.md:59/166 make headless OAuth a non-goal with API keys as the documented headless path. No file:line in the repository must change as a consequence of the interface change, which is what this lens gates on.

finding.summary: Relaxing `seg('')` lets an empty identifier silently reach collection endpoints, not the 404 the comment promises
finding.evidence: `seg('')` now returns '' (packages/cli/src/client/url.ts:39-46), so out-of-diff callers build trailing-slash paths. Nest 11 runs Express with `strict routing` disabled, where `/…/documents/` matches the collection route: `packages/backend/src/api/v1/documents.controller.ts:34` (`@Get()` list) is what `HttpClient.getDocument('')` (packages/cli/src/client/http-client.ts:202) now hits — returning the whole workspace document list where a single-document read was named. Likewise `getCell(doc, tab, '')` (http-client.ts:352-357) resolves to `packages/backend/src/api/v1/cells.controller.ts:45` (`@Get()`), dumping every cell of the tab instead of one ref. Previously both were refused before the request went out. Only the *workspace* segment truly 404s (`/workspaces//…` cannot match `:workspaceId`); identifier segments do not. Fix likely belongs in the new code: keep the empty segment allowed only for `config.workspace` (e.g. a separate `wsSeg()`), and keep refusing it for document/tab/cell/key ids.

verdict.reason: The finding's premise is factually absent from the repository. `seg()` at packages/cli/src/client/url.ts:37-44 throws on the empty string ('Invalid identifier ""...') rather than returning ''; the doc comment at url.ts:30-35 states the empty segment is refused precisely because of Express non-strict routing. A repo-wide grep for another `seg` definition found only url.ts:37, and dry-run.ts (lines 1-38) defines no separate encoder. The exemption the reviewer proposes as the fix already exists: `workspaceSeg()` at url.ts:78-80 is the only route to an empty segment and applies solely to the workspace position (url.ts:84, 95). Therefore the claimed bypassing call sites cannot reach the collection routes: http-client.ts:202 (`getDocument`) and http-client.ts:355 (`getCell`) interpolate `seg(id)`/`seg(sref)`, which throw before `request()` is invoked, so no trailing-slash path is ever emitted to documents.controller.ts or cells.controller.ts.

finding.summary: New CLI hard-requires an echoed `state`, so it cannot log in against any backend that does not yet echo it (version skew)
finding.evidence: packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:203-210 rejects any `/callback` whose `state` does not match, and the code is only echoed by the backend change in packages/backend/src/auth/auth.controller.ts:130-135. `@wafflebase/cli` is a separately published npm binary (packages/cli/package.json:7-9) pointed at arbitrary servers via `--server` / `WAFFLEBASE_SERVER`, and self-hosting is documented (packages/documentation/developers/self-hosting.md:42). Against a backend deployed before this PR the redirect carries no `state`, so the browser shows `State mismatch`, the listener never settles, and `login` fails after the 30s timeout (login.ts:261-269) with a message that names the wrong cause. Nothing pins a minimum server version.

verdict.reason: The described failure mode does not exist in the code. The cited lines 203-210 are the pure `stateMatches` helper and its doc comment (login.ts:200-208), not callback rejection logic. The real handler treats a MISSING `state` as a distinct, first-checked case: login.ts:263-271 responds 400 with UNBOUND_CALLBACK_MESSAGE (login.ts:216-220), which names the version-skew cause explicitly, and immediately sets `settled` and calls `callbackReject` — so there is no 30s timeout and no misleading `State mismatch` message. The `State mismatch` branch is gated by `received !== null` (login.ts:276) and is therefore unreachable for a nonce-less callback. Version skew is also explicitly accommodated: the `--allow-unbound-callback` flag (login.ts:17-21, threaded at login.ts:62) lets the CLI complete a login against a backend that does not echo the nonce, asserted by tests at packages/cli/test/login-callback.test.ts:84-101 and 103-112. The backend is symmetrically tolerant of an older CLI (auth.controller.ts:130-132 makes the echo conditional). The claim that the CLI "cannot log in against any backend that does not yet echo it" and that the failure surfaces as a 30s timeout naming the wrong cause is factually not present.

finding.summary: Guard silently drops a `cliState` it does not like, which the new CLI then treats as an injected callback
finding.evidence: packages/backend/src/auth/github-auth.guard.ts:31-34 stores `undefined` when `cliState` is not a string matching `CLI_STATE_PATTERN` — including the ordinary Express case where the param arrives duplicated and `req.query.cliState` is an array (a proxy or a user-copied URL can produce that). The flow then completes but the controller omits `&state=` (auth.controller.ts:130-135), and the CLI listener rejects its own genuine callback (packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:203-210), hanging to the 30s timeout. A silently-degraded flow is worse here than a 400 from `/auth/github`.

verdict.reason: The claimed code is not present. `normalizeCliState` does not store/return `undefined` for a present-but-unusable `cliState`; it throws `BadRequestException` at github-auth.guard.ts:35-39 (returning `undefined` only for the absent case, line 26). The specific Express duplicated-param/array scenario the finding names is explicitly supported, not dropped: line 28 normalizes an array, line 32 accepts identical repeats, and line 40 returns the nonce; only a conflicting duplicate throws. The guard invokes this at line 70 before `createState`, so the throw propagates out of `canActivate` and `/auth/github` returns the 400 the finding says is the desired behaviour. Consequently the downstream chain (auth.controller.ts:130-132 omitting `&state=`) is reached only for a genuinely nonce-less older-CLI flow, never for a rejected malformed nonce, so the CLI listener never rejects its own genuine callback for this reason. Repo tests pin the contract: github-auth.guard.spec.ts:32 (identical duplicates accepted), :37 (conflict throws), :100-109 ("rejects a malformed cliState instead of dropping it silently"). A repo-wide grep for `cliState` found no alternate normalisation path in cli-auth.store.ts or github.strategy.ts.
